BrowserRuntimeStatus.description: Four separate booleans because they fail for four different reasons and collapsing them would hide which fix applies. `healthy` is true only after a live workspace-runtime health request: compile flags and environment presence never count as runtime health. `reason` names the first gate that said no.

BrowserSnapshot.x-cognia-wire-source: services/workspace-runtime/src/browser-service.mjs BrowserService.snapshot; mirrored by lib/browser/protocol.ts BrowserSnapshot, where blockedDomains is optional.

CodeServerActiveEditor.description: What the user is looking at. Every field is present; `path`, `selection` and `selectedText` are null when no file editor is focused (or nothing is selected). Whole-file bodies are deliberately absent. The app PII-gates this payload before it reaches a model.

CodeServerAgentResult.x-cognia-opaque-reason: The reply is whatever the companion VS Code extension returns for the verb, and the extension owns that shape (a save report, an active-editor context, or nothing at all). Narrowing it here would freeze an editor-side contract this crate does not define.

CodeServerApplyEditResult.description: `reflected` is true only when a stale open buffer was replaced through a WorkspaceEdit, so the change entered the undo stack. `opened` is false only when the file was gone or unreadable, which the caller degrades on rather than treating as an error.

CodeServerEditorDiagnostic.description: One editor diagnostic, 1-based line and column. `severity` is the narrowed vocabulary `diagnosticSeverityName` emits, not VS Code's numeric enum.

CodeServerNotifyResult.description: `kind` is the narrowed kind actually shown. An unrecognised kind reads as `info` rather than being dropped, so this echoes back what the user saw.

CodeServerOpenResult.description: The extension revealed `path`. `opened` is always true: a failure throws instead.

CodeServerRunInTerminalResult.description: `sent` reports that the text reached the terminal, not that the command succeeded: the extension host cannot read a terminal's output back. `terminal` is the reused terminal's name.

CodeServerSaveAllResult.description: A partial flush is reported rather than thrown, so `failed` names the files whose disk copy the caller must not trust.

CodeServerStatus.description: `profile` is absent only when talking to a pre-platform host during a rolling upgrade; `relayPath` never carries a credential or the host loopback port.

CompanionEndpoints.description: Where else this host can be reached. `lanBaseUrl` is null on a loopback-bound server or a host with no routable interface; `tunnelBaseUrl` is null when no tunnel is running. `fingerprint` pins the self-signed certificate.

DetectedRuntimesReport.description: Which catalogued agent runtimes this Host already has. `resolution` is the only verdict here: `installed` means the command resolved and its catalogued `--version` was read, `missing` means it is on no PATH or install root, `package-runner` means it launches through npx and its presence cannot be established without a network install, `not-local` means the runtime has no local command at all. `versionOutput` is raw probe output; the version verdict is rendered by assessRuntimeVersion() in lib/ai/agent/external/runtime-version.ts.

config.x-cognia-opaque-reason: The stored ExternalAgentConfig is owned by the external-agent domain and versioned with it; this plane owns the head/revision envelope around it, which is typed above.

FleetSnapshot.x-cognia-wire-source: crate::fleet::registry::FleetSnapshot (rename_all = camelCase), via rpc/diagnostics.rs `to_json(runtime().snapshot_for_tenant(..))`. hosts and runtimeCapabilities carry skip_serializing_if = Vec::is_empty, so both are absent — not empty arrays — on a quiet host.
FleetSnapshot.x-cognia-fixes: Previously LegacyList, which requires an ARRAY. GitStackBranchPairList.x-cognia-wire-source: Vec<(String, String)> — a Rust tuple serialises as a two-element JSON array, not an object.

HostCapabilityReport.description: What this host physically is, and which surfaces it can reach. `capabilities` is the append-only `CORE_CAPABILITY_IDS` vocabulary from lib/platform/capabilities.ts; an id a client does not recognise is a newer host, not an error.

HostFeatureLimits.description: Byte and count ceilings the host will actually enforce. Published so a client can refuse before the user commits, instead of after the host rejects.

HostFeatureManifest.description: The effective manifest: what this host offers THIS caller, already filtered by the caller's device grants. A client renders capability from this and never self-judges by command name. Deliberately open to extra properties: the manifest is versioned and additive, and a v1 host answering a v2 client must stay readable.

hostStateScope.description: The scope the host's own host-state actually lives under. A client that addresses host-state by its own pairing id asks for a namespace the host never wrote to, and every host_state_* call is refused with host_state_scope_mismatch.

HostRuntimeOperationDescriptor.description: One command the host declares it can actually serve right now. `healthy: false` with a `reason` is the honest answer a client renders as disabled-with-explanation, which is why an unhealthy operation is published rather than omitted.

HostStateActionReceipt.description: Per-action outcome. `duplicate` is a success (the idempotency key already landed), not a failure; `rejected` and `conflicted` carry the reason on `rejection`.

HostStateSnapshot.description: A cut of one host-state channel. `digest` and `cutHostSeq` are what a replica reconciles against; `state` is the channel's own payload, whose shape belongs to the channel.

HostStateStatus.description: `recovery` is load-bearing: while it is `recovering` nothing the host reports about a turn can be trusted, and `degraded` means recovery ran and failed rather than that state is fresh.

HostStateSubmitResponse.description: One receipt per submitted action, in submission order.

LarkEntryToken.x-cognia-wire-source: lark_entry::rpc_entry_issue. Two branches: kind=entry returns token+jti+expiresAt, kind=surface returns token alone — so only `token` is guaranteed.

LarkMetricAck.x-cognia-wire-source: lark_entry::rpc_metrics_record — json!({ "ok": true }). An unknown metric name is an Err, so `ok` is only ever literal true.

NullableLegacyRecord.x-cognia-opaque-reason: As LegacyRecord, for a lookup that answers null when the record is gone. Six task-workspace getters are declared `T | null` in TypeScript and return `Option` in Rust, and the client is written around that: `getWorkspaceBundle` returning null is how `ensureSessionExecutionBundle` learns to acquire a fresh bundle. Typing them as a bare object turned that ordinary, recoverable answer into a `contract_output_violation` 500 - which is what every companion hit after a host-side workspace reset or GC.

RawWorkspaceEntry.description: snake_case on the wire — the Rust side does not rename these; the client maps them via fromRawWorkspaceEntry.

ScheduledTask.description: Date fields cross the wire as ISO-8601 strings; the client rehydrates them via hydrateTask. Optional fields are omitted rather than sent as null.

ScheduledTaskPayload.description: Union whose first member is Record<string, unknown> (types/scheduler): the per-task-type payload shapes are refinements, so any object is valid on the wire.

SecretValue.x-cognia-wire-source: Option<String> from cognia_secrets::keyring_secrets::get, via rpc/chat.rs `to_json(value)`. null means the key is absent — a successful read, not an error.
SecretValue.x-cognia-fixes: Previously LegacyRecord, which requires an object. Every successful secret_store_get / keyring_secret_get response is a bare string or null, so the enforced output contract rejected all of them with contract_output_violation.

SessionPage.description: One page of sessions. Two data planes serve `session_list` and they page differently: the Rust direct store (`companion_api/store.rs::SessionPage`) counts the whole table and returns `total` + `nextOffset`, while the indexed bridge (`lib/companion/desktop-message-source.ts::readSessionPage`) reads one row past the page and returns `next_offset` + `has_more` rather than paying for a full count. `rows` is the only field both always send, and the consumer type (`lib/claude/ipc.ts::SessionListPage`) already declares the rest optional. Requiring `total` and naming only `nextOffset` described neither implementation: it made every bridge-served `session_list` a 500 `contract_output_violation` the moment the command became device-reachable.

total.description: Whole-table count. Direct store only; the bridge omits it.

nextOffset.description: Direct store's next-page cursor (camelCase via serde `rename_all`).

next_offset.description: The bridge's next-page cursor. Same meaning as `nextOffset`, different spelling, because the two planes were written apart.

has_more.description: Bridge only: whether a row existed past this page.

SessionTimelinePage.description: `hasMore` and `nextCursor` are the only correct way to page; item counts are capped by `transcript_capabilities.maxTimelinePageSize`.

SessionTurnMessagesPage.description: `approximateBytes` is what the host measured against `maxTurnMessagePageBytes`, so a short page is a byte-budget cut rather than the end of the turn. `hasMore` says which.

SidecarStatus.x-cognia-wire-source: crate::claude::commands::SidecarStatus — derives Serialize with NO rename_all, and has exactly one field.

SyncDelta.description: One table's delta. `rows` are upserts and `deleted_ids` are tombstones; both share the `next_since` cursor space so an upsert and a deletion each cross the wire exactly once. `has_more` is set only by paged tables, and the caller keeps pulling while it is true.

TaskExecution.description: Date fields cross the wire as ISO-8601 strings; the client rehydrates them via hydrateExecution.

TerminalHostStatus.x-cognia-wire-source: crate::terminal_host_bridge::TerminalHostStatus (serde rename_all = camelCase). `descriptor` is skipped for the remote arms — provisioning a device descriptor has no remote path.

TerminalKilledPidList.x-cognia-wire-source: Vec<u32> from cognia_terminal::commands::terminal_kill_port — the PIDs actually signalled, possibly empty when nothing was listening.

TerminalProfileSyncResult.x-cognia-wire-source: rpc/terminal.rs `terminal_host_sync_profiles` — how many profiles the device now owns on the host.

TerminalSession.x-cognia-wire-source: cognia_terminal::host::HostSessionInfo (serde rename_all = camelCase), returned by rpc/terminal.rs via DispatchHost::terminal_list_all. Option fields carry no skip_serializing_if, so they are always present as null — the two ssh_host_key_* fields are the exception and do skip.

TerminalSessionParticipant.x-cognia-wire-source: cognia_terminal::host::SessionParticipant (serde rename_all = camelCase). `deviceId` carries no skip_serializing_if, so it is always present and null for the local desktop.

TmuxSession.description: `attached` is derived from tmux's `session_attached` client COUNT, so two attached clients is still true. `createdAt` is unix seconds, the unit tmux reports.

TranscriptCapabilitiesV1.description: The paging and size budget this host will honour. A client that pages past these gets a refusal, so it reads them first rather than discovering them one rejection at a time.

TranscriptMessage.description: `parts` is the AI-SDK UIMessage part union and is owned by that package, so it is not narrowed here. Everything around it is.

TranscriptTimelineItem.description: One timeline row. `kind` selects the variant and the fields that come with it; the shared head is `itemKey` / `revision` / `startedAt`. Left open so a newer host's variant fields survive an older client.

PiExtensionVerdict.description: Whether the bundled Cognia Pi extension on this Host is the one Cognia shipped. Pi ships no permission prompts of its own, so the extension that applies Cognia's matrix to its native read/edit/write/bash tools is a precondition for a session, not a diagnostic. Every refusing status is reported distinctly because "never shipped", "tampered" and "unpinned" are different sentences to whoever has to fix it.

WorkspaceRootsReport.description: Directories this Host will browse. `source` says why a root is allowed and therefore where it can be changed: `desktop-project` is registered by the active desktop project, `headless-workspaces-dir` is COGNIA_WORKSPACES_DIR and is fixed when the server starts.

SftpEntry.description: One entry on the remote machine. `size` is bytes, `modified` is the SFTP mtime in unix seconds and is absent when the server did not report one, and `permissions` is the raw mode word rather than a rendered string, because the client renders it and the server's own words are the only truth about it.

connector_enqueue_outbound.description: What the host did with the relayed reply (ADR-0131). `reused` is true when the idempotency key matched an existing job — i.e. this was a retry replay, not a second send.

connectors_onebot_probe.description: Reverse-WS OneBot clients currently dialed in to the in-app server.

sftp_list_dir.description: One directory on the remote machine. `.` and `..` are dropped where they are read, so this is entries only.

sftp_stat.description: One entry on the remote machine.

sftp_realpath.description: The path as the remote machine resolves it, symlinks included. The one place a client learns where a relative path actually lands.

sftp_create_dir.description: The remote machine accepted the change. There is nothing else to report: a failure arrives as an error envelope carrying the server's own words.

sftp_rename_entry.description: The remote machine accepted the change. There is nothing else to report: a failure arrives as an error envelope carrying the server's own words.

sftp_delete_entry.description: The remote machine accepted the change. There is nothing else to report: a failure arrives as an error envelope carrying the server's own words.

sftp_download_open.description: An approved download. `chunkBytes` is what the host will serve per read, negotiated here rather than assumed by the client, and `size` is what the remote machine reported at open.

sftp_download_read_chunk.description: One chunk of the file, base64 encoded. `eof` is true when the server returned fewer bytes than asked for, which is how a read loop stops. A short read mid-file is legal SFTP and the host loops over it, so a short answer here really is the end.

sftp_download_close.description: The handle is gone. Closing one that already expired reports the same thing, because the caller's intent is satisfied either way.

sftp_upload_open.description: An approved upload. `writeHead` is where the host will start writing, taken from what is already on the remote machine rather than from the client's memory of what it sent.

sftp_upload_write_chunk.description: The host's write head after this chunk, which is where the next one goes and where a resume starts. The client never names an offset the host did not reach.

sftp_upload_commit.description: What is actually on the remote machine now. `size` is re-read from the machine rather than reported from the write head, so a file something else also wrote is described truthfully. `complete` is that size measured against what the client declared at open.

sftp_upload_abort.description: The handle is gone. The partial file is deliberately left where it is: removing it would be a delete nobody asked for, and those bytes are what a later resume starts from.

sftp_session_close.description: How many pooled connections for that profile were dropped. Zero is the ordinary answer when nothing was open.
